newsitem.title: CHINA: China says MFN no 'political football'.
newsitem.headline: China says MFN no 'political football'.

text.p: China called on the United States on Thursday to give it permanent Most Favoured Nation (MFN) status and not to turn the trade privilege into a "political football".
"This annual debate cannot go on," said the official Guangming Daily in a commentary on the U.S. congressional vote backing China's MFN status for another year.
"China should be given permanent Most Favoured Nation treatment," it said in the article entitled "MFN is Not a Political Football".
The U.S. House of Representatives voted 259 to 173 on Tuesday to renew China's MFN status for another year, backing President Bill Clinton's decision in May.
China welcomed the victory, calling it a wise move that was in the interests of both countries.
But Beijing has been stepping up its campaign to avoid the annual debate over its trade status, which allows reduced duties on American imports of goods from China.
Without MFN, duties on imports from China would soar to an average of 44 percent from a current level of about six percent.
All but a handful of America's trade partners are entitled to the lower duty treatment.
